## Summary

The MCP client URL every doc and committed example specifies —
`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp/` (WITH the trailing slash) — answers `307` with
`location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`: an HTTPS->HTTP downgrade, with no HSTS to
upgrade it back. The no-slash `/mcp` returns a correct `401`. Re-reproduced 2026-08-27 from
unauthenticated probes. A 307 preserves method and body, and clients differ on whether they
retain `Authorization` across a same-host scheme change, so one that retains it puts its bearer
PAT on the wire in plaintext. The docs point AT the affected form
(`docs/mcp-client-setup.md:54`, `examples/mcp-clients/codex/config.toml:18`).

## Confirmed root cause

Proven at runtime; evidence, the discriminating experiment and the defect attribution
(caused_by fd4a-4e91-f179-4932) are in the RCA comment. Three changeable artifacts:

**A** `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:127` is a PREFIX `location /mcp` with a URI-preserving
`proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;`, so external `/mcp/` reaches the app verbatim while the app
mounts at `http_path = "/mcp"` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:524,618-627`); Starlette's default
`redirect_slashes` emits the 307. `docs/mcp-auth.md:252-271` already prescribes EXACT-MATCH
locations for this asymmetry and the template diverged from it.

**B** uvicorn is built at `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:311-317` with no `forwarded_allow_ips`, so
it defaults to `"127.0.0.1"` (`uvicorn/config.py:356-357`). The app runs in a container
(`docker-compose.yml:337`), so nginx arrives from the bridge gateway; that peer is untrusted,
`X-Forwarded-Proto https` (`rebar.conf.template:132`) is dropped, and scheme-derived absolute
URLs become `http://`. Blast radius checked and BOUNDED: RFC 9728 metadata and
`resource_metadata` come from the configured `auth_resource_server_url`
(`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:610`) and the live 401 returns them as `https`; no rebar code keys on
the peer address.

**C** The 443 server has no `add_header Strict-Transport-Security`.

## Approach

1. **Serve `/mcp/` directly instead of redirecting.** Adopt the documented exact-match pattern
   (`docs/mcp-auth.md:252-271`) against the named upstream: `location = /mcp/` and
   `location = /mcp`, both `proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp/mcp;`, keeping the existing SSE
   settings. An exact-match location with a URI on `proxy_pass` replaces the matched URI, so
   `/mcp/` arrives at the app as `/mcp`, `redirect_slashes` never fires, and no Location header
   is produced. The PREFIX `location /mcp` is retained for `/mcp/...` sub-paths.
2. **Make a plaintext Location structurally impossible.** Add `proxy_redirect http://$host/
   https://$host/;` plus the named-upstream form to the MCP locations, upgrading any `http://`
   Location an upstream might emit. Scoped to those locations because `proxy_redirect` defaults
   to `default` (derived from each location's own `proxy_pass`), so a server-level rule would
   replace it for `/review/` and `/opcert/` and could break their relative redirects.
3. **Fix the scheme derivation.** Set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS: "*"` on the `mcp` compose service.
   Verified in installed uvicorn 0.52.1: a programmatically-built `Config` defaults
   `forwarded_allow_ips=None` then reads `os.environ.get("FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS", "127.0.0.1")`
   (`uvicorn/config.py:356-357`) and wires `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` (`:527`) — so no code change
   is needed. `"*"` rather than a pinned address: the `mcp` service declares no `networks:`
   block, so the bridge gateway address is implicit and can drift, and a stale pin would
   silently re-open the downgrade while local tests passed. Trust-all is bounded because the
   port is published on host loopback with nginx the sole reachable client, and nginx sets
   `X-Forwarded-Proto https` as a LITERAL.
4. **Add HSTS.** `add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
   always;` on the 443 server. `always` is required so it is emitted on error responses — such
   as the 401 the MCP endpoint returns to an unauthenticated client.

NOT changed: `EXPECTED_URL` in `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py` and the
documented/example URLs — after step 1 the trailing-slash form is served directly over https, so
it stays canonical and `auth_resource_server_url` stays consistent with it. Production nginx on the live box is
NOT changed here: this lands the config in the repo and an operator applies it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The edge routes `/mcp/` straight to the app's `/mcp`, so no Location header is produced
      for the documented URL. Verified by a structural parse of `rebar.conf.template` asserting
      an exact-match `location = /mcp/` whose `proxy_pass` carries the app path `/mcp`.
- [x] An HSTS header with `max-age` of at least 31536000 is served on the 443 server, marked
      `always` so it reaches the unauthenticated 401. Verified by a structural parse asserting
      `add_header Strict-Transport-Security "..." always;` in that server block.
- [x] Each MCP location carries a `proxy_redirect` mapping an `http://` upstream Location to
      `https://`. Verified by a structural parse that fails if it is absent from any.
- [x] With the committed `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` in force, a `/mcp/` request through the real
      `streamable_http_app()` yields a Location whose scheme is `https`. Verified by an
      in-process ASGI test through uvicorn's `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` with an untrusted-peer
      negative control asserting `http`, plus a structural assertion that compose sets
      `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` to exactly `*`.
- [x] [non-codebase] LIVE VALIDATION — REQUIRED TO CLOSE. `curl -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp/`
      provenance: environment=production nginx edge at https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com; principal=unauthenticated caller (no credential sent); privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — GET and POST /mcp/ both return HTTP/2 401 with NO Location header and strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains. The 307 to http:// is gone. Edge behaviour is not determinable from source.
      emits NO `http://` Location and carries an HSTS header, OBSERVED against the deployed edge
      and recorded in a ticket comment with the actual response headers. Neither a passing local
      test nor a merged change satisfies this — it must be deployed and serving — so this
      depends on an OPERATOR applying the config and must not be ticked on a local render.

## Testing

RED-first; both tiers observed failing before any fix.

- `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` — structural tests over the committed nginx template
  (exact-match `/mcp/` and `/mcp` locations, `proxy_redirect` on each, HSTS with `always`) and
  over `docker-compose.yml` (`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` == `*`). No nginx binary is
  available here, so these parse committed text, as the existing
  `test_nginx_mcp_location_proxies_to_the_named_upstream` (`:154`) does. `nginx -t` is the
  operator's deploy-time check.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py` — a behavioural test over the real
  `streamable_http_app()` through uvicorn's `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` configured from the
  committed compose value, asserting the Location scheme is `https`, with an untrusted-peer
  negative control asserting `http`. Executable oracle for B.

Mutation check: re-introduce each confirmed cause (drop the exact-match locations, the
`proxy_redirect`, the HSTS header, `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`) and confirm the corresponding test
returns to RED, then restore. Run inside an OS sandbox.

## File impact

`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`, `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`,
`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py`.

## Compat / rollback

Additive: two exact-match locations ahead of the retained prefix location, two directives per
MCP location, one HSTS header, one compose env var. `/mcp` returns a 401 today and continues to;
`/mcp/` stops redirecting and starts serving. No caller depends on the 307 — it is the defect.
Rollback is a revert of the four files.

## Portability

Committed config plus tests that parse committed text. No CI provider is involved: the
structural tests run under plain `pytest` and the behavioural test is in-process ASGI with no
docker and no network. Applying the nginx change is an operator step, not a CI trigger.
